t.E558.agn: JECFA did not set an ADI for bentonite ('no ADI allocated'). Under Regulation 380/2012, which regulates the conditions of use of aluminium-containing additives, the EU removed bentonite from the permitted list after 31 May 2013, after food manufacturers reported that they no longer used it.
t.E558.eval: It is no longer authorised as a food additive in the EU: its authorisation ended on 31 May 2013 under Regulation (EU) 380/2012 (food manufacturers reported that they no longer used it). JECFA did not set an ADI.
t.E558.found.0: Its authorisation as a food additive in the EU ended on 31 May 2013; food manufacturers had reported that they no longer used it
t.E558.prod: It is obtained by crushing, drying, grinding and sieving clay extracted from open pits (by physical processing).
t.E558.summary: A clay of volcanic ash origin. Used to clarify wine and fruit juice and to prevent caking.
t.E558.what: It is a natural clay mineral containing aluminium that has been used as an anti-caking agent.
